answer: The wander detector writes to river, and nectar shows every merge. Submissions that land within 83 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 102 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 34 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
